correctness.rationale: TARGET-route disproof verified step by step. R psi(theta,phi)=psi(theta,-phi) is unitary on L2 and bounded on every Hs with R^2=I and R phi0=phi0. V1=z=cos theta is phi-independent and V2=x=sin theta cos phi satisfies cos(-phi)=cos phi, so both multipliers are R-even and R M_{Vk}=M_{Vk} R. As r(x,y,z)=(x,-y,z) is an S2 isometry, R preserves each spherical-harmonic eigenspace H_l and commutes with -Delta on H2 and with U0(t)=exp(itDelta). The Duhamel form (4) with bounded Vk has at most one C([0,T];L2) mild solution by Gronwall, so with R-even data R psi solves the same equation and coincides with psi; hence every trajectory from phi0 stays in the closed even subspace E for every T>0 and every bounded or unbounded real or complex control pair. Targets psi_{f,eps}=(phi0+eps eta)/sqrt(1+eps^2) with eta=sqrt(3/4pi) y satisfy ||eta||=1, -Delta eta=2 eta, R eta=-eta, unit norm, smoothness, and spectral-H3 distance squared (1/N-1)^2+27(eps/N)^2->0, so every H3 ball about phi0 contains unreachable targets. Change-of-variables gives <eta,f>=0 for all f in E, and Cauchy-Schwarz gives ||psi(T)-psi_{f,eps}||_L2 >= |eps|/N > 0. The quadrature script was re-executed and all checks passed (norms 1 to 1e-9, <c0,eta>~6.6e-18, H3 distances and odd lower bounds for eps in {0.5,0.1,0.01}). No essential inference, boundary condition, or computation fails; the argument is proof, not experiment.
